facts.statement: Gallardosaurus is classified as a pliosaurid within the family Pliosauridae.
facts.quote: Gallardosaurus was a pliosaurid, a member of the family Pliosauridae

facts.statement: The genus Gallardosaurus was formally described as a separate genus in 2009.
facts.quote: In 2009, MNHNCu P3005 was described as a separate genus, Gallardosaurus.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen was discovered in 1946 by Cuban farmer Juan Gallardo near Viñales in northwestern Cuba.
facts.quote: The specimen had been discovered in 1946 by Cuban farmer Juan Gallardo about 8 km east of Viñales, Pinar del Río, northwestern Cuba.

facts.statement: The genus name Gallardosaurus honors the fossil's discoverer, Juan Gallardo.
facts.quote: The generic name is derived from the specimen MNHNCu P3005's discoverer, Juan Gallardo

facts.statement: The species name iturraldei honors the paleontologist Dr. Manuel Iturralde-Vinent.
facts.quote: The species name G. itturraldei is derived from the name of the geotectonist and paleontologist Dr. Manuel Iturralde Vinent.

facts.statement: Gallardosaurus had a broad, low skull equipped with long, pointed teeth.
facts.quote: The skull was broad and not tall, with long pointed teeth.

facts.statement: Evidence of unfused vertebrae indicates the known specimen was a juvenile when it died.
facts.quote: The lack of fusion in some of the vertebrae suggests the individual was not fully grown when it died.

facts.statement: Fossils of Gallardosaurus come from the Late Jurassic (Oxfordian) Jagua Formation in western Cuba.
facts.quote: Gallardosaurus was found in middle-late Oxfordian-age (Late Jurassic) rocks of the Jagua Formation of western Cuba.

facts.statement: Gallardosaurus lived between 159 and 154.8 million years ago during the Oxfordian stage.
facts.quote: Time range: Oxfordian to Oxfordian (159 to 154.8 million years ago)

facts.statement: Researchers suggest Gallardosaurus likely migrated seasonally across the Caribbean Sea and primarily ate nectonic fish.
facts.quote: G. iturraldei would probably have seasonally migrated across the Caribbean Seaway, and would have preyed mostly on nectonic fish that dwelt in the region in which it existed.

facts.statement: Gallardosaurus inhabited shallow waters approximately 10 to 12 meters deep.
facts.quote: The water depth was shallow, perhaps 10 to 12 m deep, and oysters and algae colonized the sea bottom.

facts.statement: Gallardosaurus was a marine predator with a short neck that lived during the Mesozoic Era.
facts.quote: Gallardosaurus fue un pliosáurido, un grupo de reptiles marinos depredadores de cuello corto que vivieron durante la Era Mesozoica.

facts.statement: Other members of the Pliosauridae family include Hauffiosaurus, Kronosaurus, Peloneustes, Liopleurodon, Brachauchenius, and Pliosaurus.
facts.quote: Otros miembros del grupo incluyen a Hauffiosaurus, Kronosaurus, Peloneustes, Liopleurodon, Brachauchenius y Pliosaurus.

facts.statement: It is hypothesized that G. iturraldei migrated seasonally through the Caribbean Sea and hunted nectonic fish.
facts.quote: G. iturraldei probablemente habría emigrado de manera estacional a través de la vía marítima del Caribe, y habría atacado principalmente peces nectónicos que habitaban en la región en que existió.

facts.statement: The habitat of Gallardosaurus consisted of shallow water, perhaps 10 to 12 meters deep, colonized by oysters and algae.
facts.quote: La profundidad del agua era poco profunda, tal vez 10 a 12 metros (33 a 39 pies) de profundidad, y las ostras y algas colonizaron el fondo del mar.
